properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued August 28 at 9:32PM CDT until August 28 at 10:15PM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX

extending from near Bader to near Somerset, moving southwest at 30

Lytle, Somerset, Natalia, Lacoste, D'Hanis, Noonan, Quihi, Dunlay,
Mico, Pearson, Sea World, Bader, Lackland AFB, Cliff, and New

building.

properties.instruction:

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued August 28 at 9:09PM CDT until August 29 at 12:15AM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
FFWEWX

The National Weather Service in Austin/San Antonio has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northern Bexar County in south central Texas...
South Central Comal County in south central Texas...

* Until 1215 AM CDT.

* At 909 PM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
2 and 3 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of
1 to 2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
San Antonio, Schertz, Converse, Universal City, Live Oak, Selma,
San Antonio Int Airport, Randolph AFB, Leon Valley, Helotes, Kirby,
Alamo Heights, Windcrest, Terrell Hills, Garden Ridge, Shavano
Park, Hollywood Park and Olmos Park.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued August 28 at 9:55PM EDT by NWS Wakefield VA
properties.description:
A Marine Weather Statement has been issued for the following areas...
Chesapeake Bay from Little Creek VA to Cape Henry VA including the
Chesapeake Bay Bridge Tunnel...
Chesapeake Bay from New Point Comfort to Little Creek VA...
James River from JRB to HRBT, Including the Elizabeth River...

At 952 PM EDT, a marine weather observations reported a wind shift
associated with a frontal boundary crossing the area, producing
winds to around 25 knots. This front was located near Thimble
Shoals, moving south at 20 knots.  These gusty northerly winds
should last for the next couple of hours and then diminish to around
10 kt overnight.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, and lightning strikes. Boaters should seek safe harbor
immediately until this storm passes.
properties.area: Chesapeake Bay from New Point Comfort to Little Creek VA; Chesapeake Bay from Little Creek VA to Cape Henry VA including the Chesapeake Bay Bridge Tunnel; James River from JRB to HRBT, Including the Elizabeth River

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 28 at 8:36PM CDT until August 30 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Indianapolis IN
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Indiana...Illinois...

Wabash River from Hutsonville to Vincennes.

.Minor flooding continues on the Wabash River from Hutsonville down
to Vincennes. The river has crested. Flooding should come to an end
on the Wabash over the weekend.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Wabash River at Vincennes.

* WHEN...Until Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, Agricultural lands and some oil fields
flood.  Several township roads about 1.25 miles south of St.
Francesville and River Road between Billett Road and Lincoln
Memorial Bridge in Lawrence County are flooded.  Extensive flooding
of Kimmell Park at Vincennes.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:45 PM CDT /8:45 PM EDT/ Friday the stage was 17.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:45 PM CDT /8:45 PM EDT/ Friday was 18.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
tomorrow evening and continue falling to 4.5 feet Monday,
September 07.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.7
feet on 06/12/1980.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Flooding is occurring. Most flood related deaths occur in
automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips, or
low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement will be issued Saturday morning at 1015 AM CDT
/1115 AM EDT/.
properties.area: Lawrence, IL; Wabash, IL; Knox, IN
